title: Lines at Sixty Degrees: The Jordan Factors of Matsuo Algebras
content: For each Matsuo algebra in the Gorshkov–Mamontov–Staroletov classification, we prove that the Frobenius radical is the least ideal with Jordan quotient and identify the factor over ℚ. This solves both parts of their Problem 5.1 for the two infinite families and seven exceptional cases; scalar extension gives the factors over every field of characteristic zero. The argument uses a geometric characterization: a finite connected real Matsuo algebra at parameter 1/2 has Jordan quotient by its Frobenius radical if and only if its Fischer space is realized by a reflection-closed set of lines over ℝ, ℂ or ℍ, with pairwise angles 60° and 90°. The quotient map sends each axis to its rank-one orthogonal projector. Rational descent distinguishes the E₆ factor: it is the algebra of endomorphisms self-adjoint for ⟨1,1,1,1,1,3⟩, not Sym₆(ℚ). We give explicit radical generators and extend the classification to connected locally finite Fischer spaces. For the symplectic family, incidence with quadratic forms gives quotient coordinates and radical generators at both nontrivial degenerations of the Frobenius form, including non-Jordan quotients.
